authorizing_record: guillermomolina/protos#727 (PERF016, child of PERF010-B / guillermomolina/protos#722). PERF015 (guarded represented selection for canonical Boolean true/false) and the PERF016 semantic Integer-family guarded represented selection are already structurally validated in the product repository and are not under test here; this Evidence Unit owns their combined post-Step-3 controlled timing checkpoint. The identities and lineage below are supplied task input: this repository does not inspect guillermomolina/protos or guillermomolina/protos-project-docs to derive them and does not reinterpret PERF015/PERF016 product semantics.
causal_question: What is the combined steady-state timing effect of PERF015 + PERF016 on (a) the retained common benchmark driver, observed through each workload's workload-control variant, and (b) each common canonical workload, when the exact pre-PERF015 product (CONTROL) and the exact post-PERF016 product (INTERVENTION) are built as ordinary unpatched baselines on the canonical post-adoption GraalVM 25.4.4.1.1 toolchain and timed as canonical/workload-control pairs in a counterbalanced A,B,A,B block design on one pinned CPU? This Evidence Unit collects and summarizes objective measurements only; it does not classify Step 3 (STEP_3_TIMING_CLASS) or route the result (STEP3_NEXT_ROUTING).

commits_between_endpoints.subject: PERF015: admit canonical Boolean to guarded structured selection
PERF016: admit semantic Integer family to guarded represented selection

targeted_product_operations.perf015: guarded represented selection for canonical true/false on the existing canonical Boolean control behaviors ifTrue, ifFalse, ifTrueIfFalse, and, or
targeted_product_operations.perf016: guarded represented selection for the semantic Integer family; the common driver sends explicitly targeted are count > 0 and count - 1; authoritative D013 selection/provenance is cached by Integer family, selector, entered Context, Prelude and selection Assumption rather than by Integer receiver identity; no arithmetic or comparison primitive is added at the send site

product_lineage.lineage_note: The harness builds each endpoint from its exact 40-hex revision at depth 1 and therefore cannot re-derive commit ancestry. It does verify, per built image, the exact revision label, the exact pom version, the byte-identity of every measured workload source and the canonical toolchain identity.

patches_applied_note: Both roles are ordinary baseline products built by the unchanged DIST006-D Dockerfile from their own exact revision. No ablation patch, diagnostic patch, toolchain overlay or product-source edit is applied to either image.
toolchain_note: This block is the canonical post-adoption DIST006-D toolchain contract, reused unchanged and required to equal config/dist006d-baseline.json's toolchain block. The historical PERF014 25.3.4.1 toolchain is not used and no 25.3-versus-25.4 comparison is made here (that question belongs to UPSTREAM003/DIST006).

measurement_classes.startup: not measured; container and JVM start are outside every timed region
measurement_classes.warmup: 120 iterations per timed unit, retained separately and never merged into steady-state results
measurement_classes.steady_state: 100 iterations per timed unit, recorded after the warmup iterations in the same JVM

cpu_affinity.selection: first CPU of the current allowed cpuset (one representative physical CPU), identical for every timed unit of both roles

workload_control_policy: The established PERF010 four-workload canonical/workload-control matrix is reused unchanged. Each workload-control variant replaces exactly one workload-specific operation with `sink = 42` and retains the common benchmark driver. Because PERF015/PERF016 optimize work in that shared driver, the workload-control movement between the two revisions is a measured effect to report, not environmental noise to subtract away and discard. The four workload-controls originate from four different workload sources and are therefore preserved individually; their samples are never merged.
workload_identity_policy: Before any timing, the harness reads the exact canonical source bytes of every workload from BOTH built images and fails closed (WORKLOAD_SOURCE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH) unless the SHA-256 of the canonical source, and of the generated workload-control source, is identical between the two images. Source identity is never inferred from Git history.
block_order_note: Deterministic counterbalanced design, four blocks, no randomness. Block A: CONTROL runs first, INTERVENTION second. Block B: INTERVENTION runs first, CONTROL second. Within each role the canonical variant and its workload-control variant are timed adjacently. Block identity is retained in the raw evidence.

control_variant_effect.formula: control_variant_effect_ns = control_workload_control_median_ns - intervention_workload_control_median_ns; control_variant_effect_percent = 100 * control_variant_effect_ns / control_workload_control_median_ns
control_variant_effect.note: Direct revision effect on the retained common driver, reported per workload, per block and as an aggregate over the four blocks.

canonical_effect.formula: canonical_effect_ns = control_canonical_median_ns - intervention_canonical_median_ns; canonical_effect_percent = 100 * canonical_effect_ns / control_canonical_median_ns
canonical_effect.note: Direct revision effect on each canonical workload. A microbenchmark result, never a whole-language claim.

paired_control_effect.formula: canonical_improvement_ns = canonical_effect_ns; control_movement_ns = control_variant_effect_ns; paired_control_effect_ns = canonical_improvement_ns - control_movement_ns; paired_control_effect_percent = 100 * paired_control_effect_ns / control_canonical_median_ns
paired_control_effect.note: The established PERF014 paired-control residual. A positive value means the canonical workload improved beyond the movement already explained by its common driver/workload-control variant. A near-zero value is NOT evidence that Step 3 had no effect: when Step 3 improves the shared driver equally in the canonical and workload-control variants, the subtraction intentionally removes that common improvement.

order_effect_method: The established PERF014 bounded range-separation method, applied independently to the per-block percentage series of each measurement view: the A-order block values and the B-order block values are compared; DETECTED if the two ranges do not overlap, NOT_DETECTED if they overlap, INCONCLUSIVE if either order has fewer than two blocks. No statistical model is introduced.

stationarity.method: first-quarter (steady samples 0-24) versus last-quarter (steady samples 75-99) median of every 100-sample steady timed unit
stationarity.policy: Reported only. Noisy blocks are never silently discarded and no pass/fail threshold is derived from MAD or stationarity.

classification.note: The harness collects and summarizes objective measurements; classification is a later interpretation step performed against the retained raw evidence and routed through PERF010-B / guillermomolina/protos#722. No percentage or factor threshold for those classes is defined anywhere in this harness.

smoke.note: Admission and correctness gate over both exact products. Its tiny-scale timing pass exercises the reference code path and its timings are neither printed nor retained.
